payload.question_text: Which task-to-model matches are correct? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: text-embedding-3-small is an embedding model. Embedding models are built for semantic vector representations.

options.error_type: Confuses chat model with embedding model
options.rationale: GPT-4.1 is optimized for real-time chat and customer support. Embeddings require an embedding model such as text-embedding-3-small.
options.better_fit: Choose GPT-4.1 for fast interactive chat at scale.

feedback.intrinsic: Search by meaning would not be matched to the model type built for semantic vectors.
feedback.instructional: Task type matters. Use embedding models for semantic vector representations and GPT-4.1 for real-time chat.

options.rationale: GPT-5.1-codex is listed as a recommended model type for coding. It supports the coding task category.
Phi-4-multimodal-instruct is listed for multimodal work. Multimodal chat can include images, audio, and video.

payload.explanation: Correct. Each selected pairing matches the model type to the task it is recommended for.

payload.question_text: Which model is described as an Anthropic frontier-level model?

options.rationale: GPT-5.x is optimized for reasoning, planning, and agentic workflows. It is not the Anthropic model named here.
options.better_fit: Choose GPT-5.x for structured logic, multi-step reasoning, and adjustable thinking levels.

feedback.intrinsic: A team needing the stated Anthropic option would begin evaluating the wrong family.
feedback.instructional: Keep the model names distinct: Claude Opus 4.5 is the Anthropic frontier-level choice.

options.rationale: Claude Opus 4.5 is described as an Anthropic frontier-level model. It is intended for sophisticated agents and difficult reasoning tasks.

options.error_type: Confuses general-purpose model with frontier agent model
options.rationale: Mistral Large 3 is a general-purpose model that balances quality, throughput, cost, and latency. It is not described as Anthropic’s frontier-level model.
options.better_fit: Choose Mistral Large 3 for balanced multilingual drafting or business-report work.

feedback.intrinsic: The selection would emphasize balance rather than the specified frontier-level capability.
feedback.instructional: Mistral Large 3 is a different model with a different focus. The Anthropic frontier-level model is Claude Opus 4.5.

options.error_type: Confuses real-time chat model with frontier model
options.rationale: GPT-4.1 is optimized for responsive, high-volume chat. It is not the Anthropic frontier-level model.
options.better_fit: Choose GPT-4.1 for real-time chat, customer support, and interactive applications.

feedback.intrinsic: The choice would favor fast scale instead of the requested sophisticated-agent work.
feedback.instructional: GPT-4.1 and Claude Opus 4.5 solve different needs. The latter is the frontier-level Anthropic option.

payload.explanation: Correct. Claude Opus 4.5 is the Anthropic frontier-level model in this set.

payload.question_text: Text-embedding-3-small is built mainly for generating chat replies.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: A search-by-meaning feature could be designed around the wrong task type.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Embedding models represent meaning as vectors. Use chat models when the main task is generating conversational replies.

payload.explanation: Correct. text-embedding-3-small is built for semantic vector representations, not primarily chat replies.

payload.question_text: Claude Opus 4.5 can suit complex code reasoning and multi-step computer-use tasks.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: That choice could steer a long, complex task toward a model selected for a different strength.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Claude Opus 4.5 is suited to sophisticated agents, difficult code reasoning, and multi-step computer-use tasks.

payload.explanation: Correct. Complex code reasoning and multi-step computer use are stated strengths of Claude Opus 4.5.

payload.question_text: Which uses fit Mistral Large 3? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Mistral Large 3 is suitable for multilingual drafting. This is one of its stated general-purpose uses.
Mistral Large 3 can support structured business report generation. This fits its balance of quality and efficient throughput.
Mistral Large 3 can fit mid-latency agent tasks. It is positioned for balanced cost and performance.

options.error_type: Confuses Mistral Large 3 with GPT-4.1 focus
options.rationale: Mistral Large 3 has broader general-purpose uses than customer chat alone. Real-time customer support is a stated strength of GPT-4.1.
options.better_fit: Choose GPT-4.1 for real-time chat and high-volume customer support.

feedback.intrinsic: A team could unnecessarily limit a balanced general-purpose model to one narrow workload.
feedback.instructional: Mistral Large 3 supports several kinds of work. GPT-4.1 is the model optimized for speedy support chat.

payload.explanation: Correct. These are stated uses for Mistral Large 3’s balanced general-purpose capabilities.

options.rationale: An endpoint is created when a configured model is deployed. It is not a group of related models.
options.better_fit: Use this phrase when describing how an application calls a deployed model.

feedback.intrinsic: This would make it harder to compare related model choices before deployment.
feedback.instructional: Separate the group from the deployment: a family is related models, while deployment makes one configured model available.

options.text: A group sold directly by Azure
options.rationale: Models sold directly by Azure are one catalog source. A family is defined by shared lineage, not by who sells it.
options.better_fit: Use this when comparing Azure-sold models with partner or community models.

feedback.intrinsic: You could overlook related models that come from a different catalog source.
feedback.instructional: Provider source and model lineage answer different questions. A family describes related architecture or history.

options.error_type: Confuses a family with model input
options.rationale: A prompt is input sent to a model. It is not a collection of related models.
options.better_fit: Use this when describing a request sent to a model.

feedback.intrinsic: You would be naming the request instead of the group of models.
feedback.instructional: Remember that a family groups models; a prompt supplies input to one model.

options.rationale: A model family contains related models that share architecture or lineage. Members can still differ in size, capability, specialization, or version.

payload.explanation: Correct. A family groups related models, even when members differ in size or capability.

payload.question_text: Mistral Large 3 is designed only for high-volume, low-latency production chat.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: That choice could restrict a model’s use to fast chat even when multilingual drafting or business reports are needed.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: The high-volume, low-latency focus describes GPT-4.1. Mistral Large 3 is broader and balances several trade-offs.

payload.explanation: Correct. Mistral Large 3 is a general-purpose model that balances quality, throughput, cost, and latency.

payload.question_text: Foundation models are large pretrained models that can provide general capabilities out of the box.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: That choice would rule out a ready-to-deploy base model for a general task.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Foundation models are large pretrained models. They can be deployed immediately or customized through fine-tuning.

payload.explanation: Correct. Foundation models already provide general language, reasoning, or multimodal capabilities.

options.rationale: GPT-5 model-family availability is currently restricted by registration. It is not the all-user option.
options.better_fit: Choose GPT-5.x when registration is available and multi-step reasoning or planning is needed.

feedback.instructional: Availability matters during selection. GPT-4.1 is available to all Foundry users, while GPT-5.x requires registration.

options.rationale: Claude Opus 4.5 is identified for frontier-level complex work. The all-user availability statement applies to GPT-4.1.
options.better_fit: Choose Claude Opus 4.5 for long-context complex code reasoning or computer-use tasks.

feedback.intrinsic: The team might mistake a capability description for the specific availability note.
feedback.instructional: Keep availability separate from capability. GPT-4.1 is the model explicitly available to all Foundry users.

options.rationale: GPT-4.1 is stated as available to all Foundry users. It is also optimized for responsive chat at scale.

options.error_type: Confuses catalog availability with all-user availability
options.rationale: Mistral Large 3 is a balanced general-purpose catalog model. The all-user availability statement names GPT-4.1 instead.
options.better_fit: Choose Mistral Large 3 for multilingual drafting or balanced quality, cost, and latency.

feedback.intrinsic: The team could confuse being in the catalog with the stated all-user access detail.
feedback.instructional: Catalog presence and the all-user availability note are different. The noted model is GPT-4.1.

payload.explanation: Correct. GPT-4.1 is the model explicitly available to all Foundry users.

payload.question_text: Which are strengths of GPT-5.x? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: GPT-5.x is optimized for multi-step reasoning. This supports work that needs several connected reasoning steps.
Structured logic and planning are stated strengths of GPT-5.x. These strengths suit complex, organized work.
This is the main optimization of GPT-4.1. GPT-5.x is described for reasoning, logic, planning, and agentic workflows.
options.better_fit: Choose GPT-4.1 for real-time chat and high-volume production workloads.

feedback.intrinsic: Choosing for this reason could slow a busy customer-support experience.
feedback.instructional: Match GPT-5.x to reasoning-heavy work. Match GPT-4.1 to speed, efficiency, and low-latency scale.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: A fast interactive workload could be matched to a model chosen for deeper reasoning instead.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: GPT-4.1 is optimized for speed, efficiency, and low-latency inference, especially at production scale.

payload.explanation: Correct. These strengths make GPT-4.1 suitable for responsive, high-volume applications.

payload.question_text: GPT-5.x is available to all Foundry users without registration.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: A team could plan around a model family before confirming that it is available to them.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: GPT-5.x currently requires registration. GPT-4.1 is the model stated as available to all Foundry users.

metadata.unit_slo: Choose a model approach for a task and explain how Foundry evaluates models.

evaluation_context.goal: Produce an excellent, source-faithful learner session while preserving all deterministic correctness, identity, and sequence constraints.
evaluation_context.source_fidelity_goal: Independently verify the hard-gated edited challenger against the supplied source material. Reject unsupported facts, answers, explanations, feedback, or terminology changes; do not edit the artifact.

criteria.factual_fidelity: Every claim and answer is faithful to the supplied source.
criteria.answer_unambiguity: Each item has one defensible answer under its instructions.
criteria.distractor_plausibility: Distractors are credible without becoming defensible answers.
criteria.misconception_quality: Wrong choices diagnose realistic learner misconceptions.
criteria.cognitive_progression: The ordered session builds understanding at a coherent pace.
criteria.mechanic_rhythm_variation: Mechanics vary naturally without disruptive repetition.
criteria.scenario_authenticity: Scenarios resemble credible decisions or tasks.
criteria.feedback_usefulness: Feedback explains the governing concept and next step.
criteria.difficulty_appropriateness: Difficulty matches the stated audience and session position.
criteria.terminology_consistency: Terms are used consistently with the source and across items.
criteria.overall_learner_experience: The exact final sequence is coherent, varied, and instructive.

sources.input_id: 8. Get started with generative AI and agents in Azure.md
sources.location: sources/8. Get started with generative AI and agents in Azure.md

evidence.statement: The keyed answers and rationales consistently match the supplied source: text-embedding-3-small is for embeddings, GPT-5.1-codex is listed for coding, Claude Opus 4.5 is the Anthropic frontier-level model, Mistral Large 3 has the stated balanced uses, and GPT-4.1 is explicitly available to all Foundry users.
Each multiple-choice and true/false item has a single defensible key under the supplied source and its instructions; the multi-select keys correspond exactly to the explicitly listed matches or uses.

Most distractors are credible category or model-family confusions, especially in the model-family and availability items. However, absolute wording such as “only” makes some distractors easy to reject without understanding the concept.

Wrong options diagnose realistic confusions: embedding versus chat models, provider source versus model lineage, GPT-5.x reasoning versus GPT-4.1 latency, and Mistral Large 3 versus GPT-4.1 workload fit.

The sequence moves from remembering and basic true/false recognition to more true/false recognition, but it never reaches application or evaluation. The declared SLO also includes explaining how Foundry evaluates models, which is not assessed anywhere.

The exact ordered mechanic pattern is multiple choice, multiple choice, true/false, true/false, repeated three times across all 12 items. This creates a predictable and formulaic rhythm rather than natural variation.

Stems vary between single-select, select-all, and true/false formats, but the wording repeatedly uses “Which,” “What,” or a direct declarative statement and the same two-by-two mechanic grouping repeats throughout.

All 12 prompts are decontextualized recall or recognition checks. None presents a credible workload, constraint, model-comparison result, or practitioner decision requiring the learner to choose and justify an approach.

Feedback generally names the governing distinction and a better fit, such as embedding models for semantic vectors versus GPT-4.1 for chat, and GPT-5.x reasoning versus GPT-4.1 low latency. Correct-answer explanations are usually concise but rarely provide a next-step decision rule.

Remembering and understanding are reasonable for a Level 1 unit, but the entire session remains at those levels despite the SLO wording “choose” and “explain,” so it is too easy to demonstrate applied model selection or evaluation understanding.
Model names and distinctions are used consistently across items: model family, foundation model, embeddings, GPT-4.1, GPT-5.x, Claude Opus 4.5, and Mistral Large 3 retain stable meanings and labels.

The artifact is source-faithful and internally coherent for basic model facts, but the full sequence is repetitive, entirely recognition-based, lacks authentic decisions, and omits the evaluation half of the stated learning objective.

critical_defects.summary: The session does not assess the SLO requirement to explain how Foundry evaluates models.

evidence.statement: The source describes benchmarks, leaderboards, comparisons and filters, NLP metrics, AI-assisted metrics, and evaluators, but none of the 12 learner items tests any of these concepts.

critical_defects.summary: The exact sequence repeats a rigid two-multiple-choice/two-true-false cycle three times.

evidence.statement: Question types by order are multiple_choice, multiple_choice, true_false, true_false, then the same four-item pattern repeats twice.

largest_gap.summary: The session covers model facts but not the stated model-evaluation objective or applied decision making.

evidence.statement: The unit SLO is to choose a model approach for a task and explain how Foundry evaluates models. The artifact contains only model-name, capability, availability, family, and foundation-model recall checks; it contains no benchmark, leaderboard, metric, evaluator, or workload-decision item.

largest_gap.repair_instruction: Add a short source-grounded evaluation block after the model-selection practice: include at least one applied task-to-model decision and one item distinguishing benchmarks, comparisons/filters, NLP metrics, AI-assisted metrics, and evaluators, including that evaluators detect and score issues but do not resolve them. Vary the mechanics and preserve the existing keyed items.

result.concise_summary: The artifact is highly source-faithful and answerable, with useful misconception feedback, but it is mostly recall-based, has no authentic scenarios, omits the evaluation half of the SLO, and repeats the same mechanic cycle. No approved references were supplied, so confidence is reduced.
